title: Trinkets and small finds
summary: Pocket trinkets, small purses written as coin texts, and the little finds a search turns up. Coin rows roll their own amounts.

tables.name: Trinket
tables.description: Small things with a story, for pockets and for the bottom of old chests.
rows: A brass button stamped with a crown, with a bit of red thread still attached.
A tooth on a leather cord, too big to belong to anything local.
A tiny glass bottle with a cork, empty, smelling faintly of lavender.
A folded map of a harbor, with one dock circled twice.
A wooden spoon carved with the initials of three different people.
A die made of bone with a six on every side.
A silver thimble engraved with a very small bird.
A key with no lock, polished by years in somebody's pocket.
A handful of dried flowers pressed in a scrap of velvet.
A candle stub in a tin that says “Never Light Alone.”
A letter in a language nobody in the party reads, signed with a small drawing of a fish.
A pocket mirror with a crack that runs exactly through the middle of the reflection.
A little carved fox that is always slightly warmer than the hand holding it.
A ribbon with six knots, tied by someone who clearly meant something.
A coin from a country nobody can place, with a hole in the middle.
A whistle that makes no sound that people can hear, but dogs get restless.
A fish hook made of bone, wrapped in a note that says “Lucky.”
A pebble with a perfect hole in it, smooth from being worn.
A painted wooden bead with a face on it, that looks a little different every time.
A small leather pouch of colored sand, each color in its own knotted twist.

tables.name: Small find
tables.description: What a quick search turns up. Tables inside tables with quantities: sometimes more than one purse.

rows.text: A purse and something odd: {{coins-small}} and {{trinkets}}

rows: Nothing but lint, a bent nail and a bad smell.

tables.name: Where is it hidden
tables.description: A hiding place for a small treasure or a message.
rows: Under a loose floorboard beneath the bed, with a rug carefully placed on top.
Inside a hollow book on a shelf, between two thick volumes of tax law.
In the false bottom of a barrel that smells of old pickles.
Behind a loose stone in the chimney, wrapped in oilcloth.
Buried under the third apple tree from the gate.
Sewn into the hem of an old cloak that hangs by the door.
In a flowerpot with a plant that has not been watered in years.
Taped under the seat of the most uncomfortable chair in the house.
In the hollow handle of a broom that nobody ever uses.
Down the well behind a loose stone, in a box hung on a hook.
In a sealed jar at the bottom of a sack of flour.
Wrapped in a rag and hung on a hook inside the bell of the little chapel.
